message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide you can copy into your terminal or paste into a script file.  
It shows exactly what you asked for – **only the `id` and `context_attributes` fields** – while paging through results with the supplied *cursor* (`cur456`) and authenticating via your API key (`key123`).  

---

### 1️⃣ Using cURL (command line)

```bash
curl -X GET \
     https://api.test4.org/v2/community/comments/ \
     --header "Authorization: Bearer key123" \
     --data-urlencode "fields=id%2Ccontext_attributes" \
     --data-urlencode "page[cursor]=cur456"
```

#### What each part does:

| Part | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `https://api.test4.org/...` | Base URL + resource path |
| `--header "Authorization: Bearer key123"` | Passes your API key in the Authorization header |
| `--data-urlencode "fields=..."` | Tells the server you only want those two properties back |
| `--data-urlencode "page[cursor]...` | Uses the cursor value so you continue where you left off |

> ⚠️ If you’re behind a proxy or firewall, add `-x http://proxy.example.com:8080`.

---

### 2️⃣ In Python (using `requests` library)

If you prefer working inside a Python environment, here’s a minimal snippet:

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.test4.org/v2/community/comments/"
headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer key123",
}
params = {
    # Only request id & context_attributes
    "fields[id]": "",
    "fields[context_attributes]": "",   # empty values mean “include this field”
    # Pagination cursor
    "page[cursor]": "cur456",
}

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
print(response.json())
```

> 📌 Make sure you’ve installed the `requests` package first:
>
> ```bash
> pip install requests
> ```

---

### 3️⃣ Things to keep in mind

| ✅ Tip | Why it matters |
|-------|----------------|
| **Use HTTPS** | Keeps credentials safe over the network |
| **Keep your API key secret** | Never commit it to public repos or share it openly |
| **Check rate limits** | Some APIs throttle per minute/hour—look at response headers like `X-RateLimit-Limit` / `Retry-After` |
| **Handle pagination properly** | After fetching one page, look for a `next_cursor` in the JSON body and repeat until no more pages remain |
| **Validate responses** | Even though you requested only certain fields, always confirm they appear before processing further |

---

That’s all! Run either the cURL command or the Python snippet above, replace the placeholders with your real values, and you’ll receive a JSON payload containing **just the comment IDs and their associated context attributes**, starting from the point indicated by `cur456`.
